title: 1 Esdras
lead: 1 Esdras is a Greek book that retells 2 Chronicles 35–36, nearly all of Ezra and part of Nehemiah 8, in a different order and with the added story of Darius's three guards. It is in the Greek Bible and the Orthodox canon, in the Apocrypha of many Protestant Bibles, and in an appendix to the Latin Vulgate as 3 Esdras; modern Catholic Bibles leave it out.

sections.b:
The Greek Bible has two books of Esdras. Esdras B (often called 2 Esdras) is a close translation of Ezra–Nehemiah. Esdras A, called 1 Esdras in English, is a freer work. It starts with Josiah's Passover (2 Chronicles 35), runs through the fall of Jerusalem and Cyrus's decree (Ezra 1), moves the Artaxerxes letters of Ezra 4:7–24 to just after Cyrus, and then tells a contest at Darius's court, where young Zerubbabel wins by arguing that women are strongest, and truth strongest of all (1 Esdras 3:1–5:6). Darius rewards him with leave to rebuild. The book ends with Ezra's law reading (Nehemiah 8). Josephus follows it closely in Antiquities 11. Scholars debate whether it is a fragment of an older edition of Ezra or a later reworking; Zipora Talshir argues the second. Names can confuse: the Latin Vulgate calls it 3 Esdras, and the English Apocrypha's "2 Esdras" is a different book, the apocalypse also called 4 Ezra. Verse numbers in English Bibles also differ from Rahlfs' Greek edition.

Verse numbers differ between English editions, which follow the KJV Apocrypha, and Greek editions such as Rahlfs. For example, Cyrus's list of vessels is 1 Esdras 2:13–14 in the KJV but 2:9–11 in Rahlfs. This site cites 1 Esdras in the numbering of Swete's Greek text; the KJV numbers some verses differently, and the 1 Esdras pages show the KJV's own numbers beside each verse.
